title: Dialkyl ether synthesis through heteroatom homolytic substitution.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Ran paper_context.py: Data Availability says all data are in the main text or Supplementary Information (SI); no GEO/SRA/BioProject links. The only accession, Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.16996017, is the RDKit 2025.03.6 software release (an 85.6 MB source zip), not data from this study. Europe PMC supplementaryFiles call timed out, so the SI could not be retrieved.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: This is an organic chemistry methods paper (MacMillan lab and Merck): titanium plus photoredox catalysed coupling of redox-active esters with alcohols to make dialkyl ethers. Its substrate-scope table, with reaction yields, sits in figures and the SI PDF. I did not count the examples; for this kind of paper it is typically tens to low hundreds.

a1_downloadable.note: No deposited dataset. Data exist only as figures and an SI PDF (not retrieved; the Europe PMC supplement endpoint timed out). The Zenodo DOI cited is RDKit software, not study data.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: The yield for each substrate would have to be transcribed from scope figures or SI text. No machine-readable label column exists, as far as the paper text shows.

a3_inputs_present.note: Molecules appear as drawn structures and compound names, not SMILES. They would need manual redrawing or image-to-structure conversion.

a4_units_stated.note: Isolated yields in percent are standard. Taken from the paper's conventions; not checked in a file.

a5_enough_rows.note: A single-paper substrate scope is far below the 1,500-row bar (400 for classification). The exact count is not verified, so null.

a6_fits_laptop.note: Tiny, if it could be built at all.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Can't check: no data file to compare against the paper.

a8_label_provenance.note: Yields are measured experimentally (isolated or NMR, i.e. nuclear magnetic resonance, yields). Not a model output.

honest_claim_h3: Not applicable: there is no usable dataset. At best, a reaction-yield model trained on one paper's substrate scope of roughly 100 examples or fewer, all with positive results, could not generalise beyond this reaction.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use the structures of the acid and alcohol starting materials to predict the yield of the ether-forming reaction.
plain_idea.train_on: Pairs of starting materials (an acid-derived ester plus an alcohol) from the paper's substrate-scope figures. Count unknown; likely under a few hundred, and mostly successful reactions.
plain_idea.predict: Percent yield of the dialkyl ether product, as measured by the authors after each reaction.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Medicinal chemists could triage which hindered ethers are worth attempting. But this is chemistry, outside the project's biology-only scope, and one paper is far too small to train on.

ml_idea: Reaction-yield prediction from substrate structures. Not viable: the data is a small, positives-only substrate scope locked in figures and an SI PDF, and the topic is synthetic chemistry, not biology.

effort.compute_note: Not estimated; rejected at Part A.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Count the substrate-scope entries in the SI. Almost certainly under 400, and nothing is deposited as machine-readable data.

verdict_reason: Organic synthesis methods paper, outside the biology-only scope. No deposited data: the substrate scope with yields exists only in figures and an SI PDF, as drawn structures rather than SMILES, and is far too small (A1, A2, A3, A5 fail). The cited Zenodo DOI is RDKit software, not study data.
